claim.property: API credentials are sent only to the authenticated Browser Use API endpoint; provider options do not introduce a lower-privilege credential reader
claim.attacker: remote network or web-page content attacker without TLS identity for api.browser-use.com; local operator and configured provider already trusted
claim.scope: changed Browser Use provider credential and response path

assets: remote browser session with possible profile cookies
session recording and provider session ID

principals.name: local operator/daemon
principals.existing_authority: sets and reads its own process environment and cloud credential

principals.name: Browser Use API
principals.existing_authority: authorized recipient of API key, creates remote browser and stores requested profile/recording

principals.name: browser page
principals.existing_authority: controls its own content, no changed path to provider environment

principals.name: network peer
principals.existing_authority: can fail or delay transport; lacks accepted API TLS certificate

boundaries: daemon HTTPS to fixed Browser Use API host
entrypoints: HTTPS response body containing id and cdpUrl
sinks: API error text returned to same local caller

prerequisites: Browser Use API authenticated by reqwest TLS verification

chain.control: no user/page-controlled destination in new POST; custom env values are JSON serialized
chain.boundary: credential remains between authorized daemon and provider
chain.impact: no new unauthorized credential reader or injection demonstrated

evidence: cli/src/native/providers.rs:388-410 uses reqwest client with default certificate verification and header auth; it removes prior API key query-string connection URL
cli/Cargo.lock pins reqwest 0.12.28 and cli/Cargo.toml enables rustls-tls-webpki-roots
browser-use-v4-openapi.json specifies APIKeyHeader for POST and PATCH

prerequisites: provider transport stalls or stop fails

chain.reachability: new create request holds daemon state lock; existing stop helper now receives Browser Use sessions
chain.control: bounded local proxy forced no-response; no hostile deployed service boundary assumed
chain.impact: hang and cleanup loss are correctness failures, not proven security vulnerabilities

verification.authorized_scope: read-only source tracing and bounded localhost transport fixture with dummy API key; no cloud session creation or third-party account access
commands: read exact provider, caller, lockfile, and official OpenAPI source
verification.cleanup: Fixture proxy released, isolated daemon closed, dummy credential only. Target worktree clean.
limits: Static security review of changed transmission boundaries; this is not a cloud provider penetration test.

routed_non_security_defects: F2 failed stop acknowledgement and retry ownership
